learningObjectives: Explain the physiological or methodological basis of Cortical Generators.
Apply Cortical Generators to technically valid clinical interpretation.
Identify artifacts, confounds and limits that could alter conclusions.
Communicate findings without exceeding the evidence or professional scope.

mechanismMap.label: Core concept
mechanismMap.detail: Parallel apical dendrites of cortical pyramidal neurons form open fields whose postsynaptic currents can summate and propagate to the scalp.

mechanismMap.label: Mechanism
mechanismMap.detail: Radial and tangential dipoles project differently across electrode arrays. Deep, small or closed-field generators may be poorly visible despite clinically important activity.

mechanismMap.label: Clinical integration
mechanismMap.detail: Generator geometry explains why absence of a scalp EEG finding does not exclude focal pathology or seizures.

mechanismMap.label: Boundary condition
mechanismMap.detail: Assuming every cortical event is equally visible ignores orientation, depth and spatial extent.

reviewPrompts.answer: Radial and tangential dipoles project differently across electrode arrays. Deep, small or closed-field generators may be poorly visible despite clinically important activity.
Generator geometry explains why absence of a scalp EEG finding does not exclude focal pathology or seizures.
Assuming every cortical event is equally visible ignores orientation, depth and spatial extent.
Scalp EEG sensitivity is constrained by physics before interpretation even begins.
